title: Recurring unresolved limitation 'small-sample-size' across 3 independent papers
explanation: 3 independent papers (2011–2017) report an own-work limitation normalized to 'small-sample-size'. Mixed-fidelity: 3 full-text, 0 abstract-only; score corrected for the ~11x full-text detection bias = 0.631 vs uncorrected 0.631. Methodological diversity: 5 distinct methods (NOTE: diversity/time-span weighting extends beyond opportunity-criteria.md). Resolution is ASSUMED absent — no limitation-resolution relation exists in Phase 3, so 'unresolved' is unverified. CAVEAT: 'small-sample-size' is a generic methodological category; it may fail the actionability 'named object of study' bar. Example limitation statements: The total number of eligible studies focused specifically on social media use and depressive symptoms was low  | The study sample size was small, consisting of only 13 enrolled outpatients with major depressive disorder. | The study was conducted with a small sample size of 8 participants.. Papers: openalex:W2130042179; openalex:W2147085624; openalex:W2593771132.

caveats.label: Generic category
caveats.detail: The limitation category is generic and may fail the actionability bar.

consumer.headline: 3 separate teams ran into the same wall: tested on too few examples
consumer.kind_short: A problem that several independent teams ran into
consumer.kind_long: Papers describe the limits of their own work. When separate teams — who did not build on each other — keep reporting the same limit, that is a sign of a real obstacle rather than one group's bad luck.
consumer.strength_meaning: There is real evidence behind this, but it rests on a small number of papers — read them before trusting it.
consumer.why: 3 separate research teams each reported hitting this in their own work. They did not build on each other, so this is unlikely to be one group's bad luck. Their papers span 1 years. We could read 3 of them in full, which is where teams describe what actually went wrong.

caveats.label: Broadly worded
caveats.text: The problem these papers describe is worded broadly enough that they may not be running into quite the same thing.
